newsitem.title: CHINA: China congratulates Hashimoto on re-election.
newsitem.headline: China congratulates Hashimoto on re-election.

text.p: China on Thursday congratulated Ryutaro Hashimoto on his re-election as Japan's prime minister and said it hoped his new cabinet would take steps to improve and develop Sino-Japanese relations.
"We express our congratulations to Mr Ryutaro Hashimoto on his re-election," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing.
Japan's Lower House formally re-elected Hashimoto prime minister on Thursday.
"We are looking forward to the new Japanese cabinet ... taking new and practical steps to improve and develop Sino-Japanese relations," Cui said without elaborating.
Sino-Japanese ties were strained this year over a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea, which Beijing calls the Diaoyus and Tokyo the Senkakus.
A Japanese right-wing group built a makeshift lighthouse on one of the islands in July, triggering anti-Japanese demonstrations in Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Taiwan also claims the islands while activists in the British colony of Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule next year, have opposed Japan's territorial claims.
Emotions were fanned in September when a Hong Kong activist drowned after he jumped into stormy waters around the islands to demonstrate support for Chinese claims.

In October, about 300 Taiwanese and Hong Kong protesters aboard a 50-boat flotilla pierced a Japanese maritime cordon around the islands and briefly raised the flags of Beijing and Taipei on the rocky outcrops in a challenge to Tokyo.
